#

Real-World Surveillance: Applications and Challenges, 7th
@ WACV2027
UPAR Challenge Track 2: Attribute-based Person Retrieval

## News - Oct 8, 2026: Update from CPU to GPU runners: Nvidia A10 GPU, 24 GB VRAM, 20 CPU Cores, 40 GB RAM, time limit per run: 5 minutes - Oct 6, 2026: We have clarified the rules concerning post-processing and re-ranking. Please review them to ensure compliance. - Oct 2, 2026: New code & fact sheet submission deadline: **Oct 26, 2026, AoE**. Due to strict WACV deadlines, we must move up the d - eadline. - Sep 30, 2026: [Track3](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/18273/) on Human Pose Estimation is now live ## Challenge & Workshop Track 1 of the **UPAR Challenge** at the Real-World Surveillance workshop (RWS), WACV 2027. Everything about this track lives on this Codabench page: task, data, evaluation, submission format, schedule and rules. Announcements go out by email to registered participants. See also the workshop website and Tasks 2 and 3 of the UPAR Challenge. The RWS workshop welcomes both regular submissions on the topic of real-world surveillance and submissions as part of the Challenge: - [RWS Workshop](https://vap.aau.dk/rws/) - [Challenge Task 1: Pedestrian Attribute Recognition](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/18180/) - [Challenge Task 2: Attribute-Based Person Retrieval](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/18196/) - [Challenge Task 3: Human Pose Estimation](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/18273/) ## The task Find people by description. A query is not an image but a **set of attributes**, such as *adult, female, long hair, red short-sleeved top, black trousers, backpack*. For every query, rank a gallery of pedestrian images so that the people matching the description come first. Queries use the 40 binary UPAR attributes: age, gender, hair length, upper and lower body clothing length, colour and type, and accessories. The challenge builds on the UPAR dataset, which unifies the annotations of several public pedestrian datasets. The gallery comes from a hidden domain your model has never seen, so the method has to generalize. You submit **code, not rankings**. Your model runs inside the evaluation container on a hidden gallery, and only the resulting metrics are published. ## Getting started 1. Read the **Data** page and download the training data and example submission. [Starter Kit](https://github.com/speckean/UPAR-Challenge-2027) 2. Take the **example submission** as your template. It shows the functions the platform calls. 3. Put your model and weights into the submission folder, zip the **contents** of the folder so `run.py` is at the archive root, and upload it under **My Submissions**. See the **Submission** page for the API your `run.py` must expose, and the **Evaluation** page for the metrics. Submissions run in `pytorch/pytorch:2.4.1-cuda12.1-cudnn9-runtime` (Python 3.11, torch 2.4.1, torchvision, numpy, Pillow) with **no network access**. Ship everything your model needs inside the zip. ## Code submission and winner selection After the challenge deadline, participating teams are required to submit their code, models, and a short description of their method (fact sheet) by **Oct 26, 2026, AoE** to **upar.challenge@gmail.com**. A panel of experts will review the entries. The executable/source code should include trained models, training code, and necessary parameters to ensure reproducibility. Teams that do not comply are removed from the final ranking. Note: Submitted codes will not be saved on the evaluation servers. Final submission codebases provided to the organizers will be used only for reproducibility checks and winner verification, and will not be shared publicly or with other participants at any stage. ## Paper submission We strongly encourage all challenge participants to submit a technical paper to the RWS workshop. Your paper should detail your methodology, experiments, and results on the challenge dataset. Accepted papers will be presented at the workshop and published in the WACV workshop proceedings. This is an excellent opportunity to share your insights with the community and gain visibility for your work. Submission Guidelines: - Format: [WACV format](https://wacv.thecvf.com/Conferences/2026/AuthorReviewerGuides) - Submission System: [Openreview](https://openreview.net/group?id=thecvf.com/WACV/2027/Workshop/RWS) - Challenge paper deadline: **Oct 23, 2026, AoE** ## Schedule | Date | Event | | --- | --- | | Sep 21, 2026 | Challenge opens, training data available | | Oct 21, 2026, AoE | Challenge submission deadline | | Oct 23, 2026, AoE | Paper submission deadline | | Oct 26, 2026, AoE | Code & fact sheet submission deadline, code verification starts | | Jan 4/5, 2027 | RWS Workshop at WACV 2027 | ## Citation ```bibtex @inproceedings{specker2023upar, title={UPAR: Unified Pedestrian Attribute Recognition and Person Retrieval}, author={Specker, Andreas and Cormier, Mickael and Beyerer, Jurgen}, booktitle={Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision}, year={2023} } @inproceedings{cormier2023upar, title={UPAR challenge: pedestrian attribute recognition and attribute-based person retrieval-dataset, design, and results}, author={Cormier, Mickael and Specker, Andreas and Jacques, Julio CS and Florin, Lucas and Metzler, J{\"u}rgen and Moeslund, Thomas B and Nasrollahi, Kamal and Escalera, Sergio and Beyerer, J{\"u}rgen}, booktitle={2023 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision Workshops (WACVW)}, pages={166--175}, year={2023}, organization={IEEE} } @inproceedings{cormier2024upar, title={Upar challenge 2024: Pedestrian attribute recognition and attribute-based person retrieval-dataset, design, and results}, author={Cormier, Mickael and Specker, Andreas and Junior, Julio and CS, Jacques and Moritz, Lennart and Metzler, J{\"u}rgen and Moeslund, Thomas B and Nasrollahi, Kamal and Escalera, Sergio and Beyerer, J{\"u}rgen}, booktitle={Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision}, pages={359--367}, year={2024} }

# Data

## Training data

Training data and starter kit can be found here: [Starter Kit](https://github.com/speckean/UPAR-Challenge-2027)
The use of external data to fine-tune PAR is not permitted.
Pre-trained models trained on common datasets such as ImageNet, or foundation models/VLMs that were not specifically trained for PAR, are permitted.

## Attributes

40 binary attributes, in this exact order. A query is a vector of 40 values,
`1` = the person has the attribute, `0` = the person does not.

```text
 0 Age-Young                  20 LowerBody-Length-Short
 1 Age-Adult                  21 LowerBody-Color-Black
 2 Age-Old                    22 LowerBody-Color-Blue
 3 Gender-Female              23 LowerBody-Color-Brown
 4 Hair-Length-Short          24 LowerBody-Color-Green
 5 Hair-Length-Long           25 LowerBody-Color-Grey
 6 Hair-Length-Bald           26 LowerBody-Color-Orange
 7 UpperBody-Length-Short     27 LowerBody-Color-Pink
 8 UpperBody-Color-Black      28 LowerBody-Color-Purple
 9 UpperBody-Color-Blue       29 LowerBody-Color-Red
10 UpperBody-Color-Brown      30 LowerBody-Color-White
11 UpperBody-Color-Green      31 LowerBody-Color-Yellow
12 UpperBody-Color-Grey       32 LowerBody-Color-Other
13 UpperBody-Color-Orange     33 LowerBody-Type-Trousers&Shorts
14 UpperBody-Color-Pink       34 LowerBody-Type-Skirt&Dress
15 UpperBody-Color-Purple     35 Accessory-Backpack
16 UpperBody-Color-Red        36 Accessory-Bag
17 UpperBody-Color-White      37 Accessory-Glasses-Normal
18 UpperBody-Color-Yellow     38 Accessory-Glasses-Sun
19 UpperBody-Color-Other      39 Accessory-Hat
```

## Test data

The test set is hidden. It is mounted into your container, read-only, with this
layout:

```text
input_data/
├── queries.csv     one query per line: 40 comma-separated 0/1 values
├── images.csv      the gallery: one image path per line, no labels
├── images/         the image files, at the paths listed in images.csv
│   └── <dataset>/...
└── task.json       attribute names, number of queries and gallery images
```

The queries are complete descriptions: every query is the full attribute
vector of at least one person in the gallery. A gallery image is a **correct
match** for a query if all 40 of its attributes equal the query. Several
images can match the same query, and an image never matches two queries.

The gallery images are pedestrian crops of varying size and aspect ratio.

You do not have to parse these files yourself: the ingestion program does it
and hands your code the queries and the gallery in one `sample` dict. See the
**Submission** page.

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
# Evaluation

The protocol and metrics are those of the previous UPAR challenge edition
(WACV 2024). The scoring program reproduces the original evaluation script.

## What is evaluated

For every query your model returns a ranking of the **whole gallery**, best
match first. A gallery image is a correct match for a query if all of its 40
attributes equal the query.

## Metrics

| Leaderboard | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **mADM** | mean average degree of match - **the ranking metric** |
| mAP | mean average precision over the queries |
| Rank-1 | share of queries whose top result is a correct match |
| Rank-5 | share of queries with a correct match among the top 5 |
| Rank-10 | share of queries with a correct match among the top 10 |
| mINP | mean inverse negative penalty |

For one query with `R` correct matches in the gallery, at the ranks
`r_1 < r_2 < ... < r_R` of your ranking:

```text
AP  = ( 1/r_1 + 2/r_2 + ... + R/r_R ) / R
INP = R / r_R
```

`AP` rewards placing **all** correct matches early. `INP` looks only at the
hardest one: it is 1 if the last correct match directly follows the others,
and falls towards 0 the deeper you have to search for it. `mAP` and `mINP` are
the means over the queries, `Rank-k` is the share of queries with `r_1 <= k`.

### mADM - the ranking metric

`AP` is all-or-nothing: an image that differs from the query in a single
attribute counts exactly like one that differs in twenty. The **average degree
of match** (ADM) keeps the structure of `AP` but credits near misses.

For a query, the degree of match of a gallery image is the share of the 40
attributes on which image and query agree. It is normalized per query, so that
an average gallery image earns nothing and a perfect match earns 1:

```text
dom(g)  = (number of attributes where image g equals the query) / 40
ndom(g) = max( 0, (dom(g) - mean dom) / (max dom - mean dom) )      mean, max over the gallery
```

With `g_1, g_2, ...` your ranking and `r_1 < ... < r_R` again the ranks of the
correct matches:

```text
ADM = ( 1/R ) * sum over k of  ( ndom(g_1) + ... + ndom(g_{r_k}) ) / r_k
```

So at the rank of every correct match, `AP` asks *which share of the images
ranked so far is correct*, and `ADM` asks *how well do the images ranked so far
match the query on average*. A ranking that places similar-looking people
ahead of unrelated ones scores higher than one that does not, even if both
find the exact matches at the same ranks. A perfect ranking reaches 1. `mADM`
is the mean over the queries.

Reference: A. Specker, J. Beyerer, *Balanced Pedestrian Attribute Recognition
for Improved Attribute-based Person Retrieval*, 2023, and the UPAR Challenge
2024 report.

## Ties

If you return distances or similarities, equal values are ranked in gallery
order. Avoid large groups of ties, they make your result depend on that order.

## Leaderboard

Your **latest** submission is the one shown on the leaderboard, not your best.

# 评估

协议和指标采用前一届UPAR挑战赛版本（WACV 2024）的标准。评分程序复现了原始评估脚本。

## 评估内容

对于每个查询，你的模型需要返回整个库集的排名，最佳匹配排在首位。如果库集图像的所有40个属性都与查询相等，则该图像是查询的正确匹配。

## 指标

| 排行榜 | 含义 |
| --- | --- |
| **mADM** | 平均匹配度 - **排名指标** |
| mAP | 查询的平均精度均值 |
| Rank-1 | 最高排名结果是正确匹配的查询占比 |
| Rank-5 | 前5个结果中包含正确匹配的查询占比 |
| Rank-10 | 前10个结果中包含正确匹配的查询占比 |
| mINP | 平均逆负惩罚 |

对于一个查询，库集中有`R`个正确匹配，其排名为`r_1 < r_2 < ... < r_R`：

```text
AP  = ( 1/r_1 + 2/r_2 + ... + R/r_R ) / R
INP = R / r_R
```

`AP`奖励**所有**正确匹配都排在前面的情况。`INP`仅关注最难找到的匹配：如果最后一个正确匹配紧接在其他匹配之后则为1，搜索深度越深则数值越接近0。`mAP`和`mINP`是所有查询的均值，`Rank-k`是`r_1 <= k`的查询占比。

### mADM - 排名指标

`AP`是全有或全无的：与查询相差一个属性的图像与相差二十个属性的图像计数完全相同。**平均匹配度**（ADM）保持`AP`的结构但对接近匹配进行评分。

对于一个查询，库集图像的匹配度是该图像与查询相同的40个属性的占比。它按查询进行归一化，使得平均库集图像获得0分，完美匹配获得1分：

```text
dom(g)  = (图像g与查询相同的属性数) / 40
ndom(g) = max( 0, (dom(g) - 平均dom) / (最大dom - 平均dom) )      平均值、最大值取遍整个库集
```

对于排名`g_1, g_2, ...`和正确匹配的排名`r_1 < ... < r_R`：

```text
ADM = ( 1/R ) * 对k求和  ( ndom(g_1) + ... + ndom(g_{r_k}) ) / r_k
```

因此，在每个正确匹配的排名位置，`AP`问的是**到目前为止排名的图像中有多少比例是正确的**，而`ADM`问的是**到目前为止排名的图像平均匹配度如何**。将外观相似的人排在无关人员之前的排名得分更高，即使两者都在相同位置找到精确匹配也是如此。完美排名达到1分。`mADM`是所有查询的均值。

参考文献：A. Specker, J. Beyerer, *Balanced Pedestrian Attribute Recognition for Improved Attribute-based Person Retrieval*, 2023，以及UPAR挑战赛2024报告。

## 平局

如果返回距离或相似性，相等值按库集顺序排名。避免大量平局组，它们会使结果依赖于该顺序。

## 排行榜

排行榜显示的是你的**最新**提交，而非最佳提交。

pages.content:
# Submission

You upload a zip containing your model, the platform runs it against data you never see.

## The zip

Zip the **contents** of your submission folder, not the folder itself:

```bash
cd my_submission
zip -r ../my_submission.zip . -x "*/__pycache__/*" "*.DS_Store" ".git/*"
unzip -l ../my_submission.zip | head    # run.py must be at the root
```

Required at the root of the archive:

```text
run.py           your entry point
metadata.yaml    copy it unchanged from the example submission
<anything else>  weights, modules, configs
```

## The API

The ingestion program imports `run.py` and calls:

```python
def load_model() -> None:
    """Optional. Called once. Load your weights here."""

def rank_gallery(sample: dict) -> dict:
    """Called once, with all queries and the whole gallery."""
```

`sample` is:

```python
{
  "attribute_names": ["Age-Young", "Age-Adult", ...],     # the 40 names, in order
  "queries": [[0, 1, 0, 1, ...], ...],                    # Q queries x 40 values (0/1)
  "gallery": [                                            # G gallery images
    {"index": 0,
     "image": "<dataset>/images/0.jpg",                       # path as listed in images.csv
     "image_path": "/app/input_data/images/<dataset>/images/0.jpg"},   # absolute, readable
    ...
  ],
}
```

Return a dict with **exactly one** of these keys. Each holds a `Q x G` matrix
(list of lists, numpy array or tensor): row `i` belongs to `queries[i]`,
column `j` to `gallery[j]`.

| Key | Content | Ranked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"distances"` | float, how far image `j` is from query `i` | smallest first |
| `"similarities"` | float, how well image `j` matches query `i` | largest first |
| `"ranking"` | int, row `i` = all gallery indices `0..G-1`, best match first | as given |

The key states the direction of your values, so a distance is never mistaken
for a score. A bare array, NaN/Inf, a wrong shape, or a `ranking` row that is
not a permutation of `0..G-1` fail the submission with a message in the
ingestion log. Equal distances or similarities are ranked in gallery order.

The usual recipe is two steps: predict attribute probabilities for every
gallery image once, then compute the distance of every query to every image.
The example submission does exactly that, without ever building a
`Q x G x 40` tensor.

## Runtime environment

- **No network access.** Ship your weights inside the zip. Nothing is downloaded at run time.
- The image is `pytorch/pytorch:2.4.1-cuda12.1-cudnn9-runtime`: Python 3.11,
  torch 2.4.1, torchvision, numpy, Pillow. Anything else your code imports must
  travel in the zip.
- There is a wall-clock limit for the whole run. `rank_gallery()` is a single
  call, so batch your image loading and inference yourself, and print your own
  progress: it shows up in the ingestion log.
- The working directory is your submission folder, so relative paths to your
  weights work.

# 提交

您上传一个zip文件，平台使用您未曾看过的数据对其进行测试。

## Zip文件

压缩您提交文件夹的**内容**，而非文件夹本身：

```bash
cd my_submission
zip -r ../my_submission.zip . -x "*/__pycache__/*" "*.DS_Store" ".git/*"
unzip -l ../my_submission.zip | head    # run.py 必须在根目录
```

归档文件根目录需要的文件：

```text
run.py           您的入口点
metadata.yaml    从示例提交中原样复制
<其他任何文件>   权重、模块、配置
```

## API

摄取程序导入 `run.py` 并调用：

```python
def load_model() -> None:
    """可选。调用一次。在此处加载您的权重。"""

def rank_gallery(sample: dict) -> dict:
    """调用一次，包含所有查询和整个库。"""
```

`sample` 结构为：

```python
{
  "attribute_names": ["Age-Young", "Age-Adult", ...],     # 40个名称，按顺序
  "queries": [[0, 1, 0, 1, ...], ...],                    # Q个查询 x 40个值 (0/1)
  "gallery": [                                            # G个库图像
    {"index": 0,
     "image": "<dataset>/images/0.jpg",                       # images.csv中列出的路径
     "image_path": "/app/input_data/images/<dataset>/images/0.jpg"},   # 绝对路径，可读
    ...
  ],
}
```

返回一个字典，**恰好包含以下键之一**。每个键对应一个 `Q x G` 矩阵（列表嵌套、numpy数组或张量）：第 `i` 行对应 `queries[i]`，第 `j` 列对应 `gallery[j]`。

| 键 | 内容 | 排序方式 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"distances"` | 浮点数，图像 `j` 与查询 `i` 的距离 | 从小到大 |
| `"similarities"` | 浮点数，图像 `j` 与查询 `i` 的匹配程度 | 从大到小 |
| `"ranking"` | 整数，第 `i` 行 = 所有库索引 `0..G-1`，最佳匹配优先 | 按给定顺序 |

该键说明了您的值的方向，因此距离不会被误认为是得分。裸数组、NaN/Inf、错误形状或 `ranking` 行不是 `0..G-1` 的排列都会导致提交失败，并在摄取日志中显示错误信息。相等的距离或相似性按库顺序排名。

通常的做法分两步：预测每个库图像的属性概率（仅一次），然后计算每个查询到每个图像的距离。示例提交正是这样做的，无需构建 `Q x G x 40` 张量。

## 运行时环境

- **无网络访问。** 在zip中包含您的权重。运行时不下载任何内容。
- 镜像为 `pytorch/pytorch:2.4.1-cuda12.1-cudnn9-runtime`：Python 3.11、torch 2.4.1、torchvision、numpy、Pillow。您的代码导入的任何其他内容必须包含在zip中。
- 整个运行有时间限制。`rank_gallery()` 是单次调用，因此请自行批量加载图像和推理，并打印您自己的进度：这会显示在摄取日志中。
- 工作目录是您的提交文件夹，因此相对路径指向您的权重是可行的。

pages.content:
# Submission & Evaluation

Submit predicted action sequences in a ZIP archive, using only each episode's initial RGB image and instruction.

## Action format

Each action is [dx, dy, dyaw]: forward displacement, leftward displacement in the agent's **current local frame**, and yaw update in radians. Sequences may have different lengths; the JSON list ends the trajectory.


Limits: at most 64 actions per episode; hypot(dx,dy) ≤ 2.46 dataset coordinate units and |dyaw| ≤ 6.29 rad per action (evaluated modulo 2π in [−π, π)).

## ZIP layout

Put the required JSON files at the archive root. The downloadable example ZIP shows the layout and Phase 1 episode IDs; replace its illustrative actions.

| Phase |   | Required files |
| :-- | :--: | :-- |
| Phase 1 |   | val_seen.json, val_unseen.json |
| Phase 2 |   | test.json |

### JSON schema

Each file contains split and episodes. Include every phase episode_id exactly once, with an actions list:

    {
      "split": "val_unseen",
      "episodes": [
        {
          "episode_id": "20210826_40_0001_02_0",
          "actions": [[0.25, 0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0, 0.15], [0.12, -0.05, 0.0]]
        }
      ]
    }

This abbreviated example is not a complete submission.

## Evaluation metrics

The two fidelity metrics range from 0 to 1. See [demonstration.py](https://github.com/F1y1113/worldnav-challenge/blob/main/demonstration.py) for the five calculations.

| Metric |   | Direction |   | Meaning |
| :-- | :--: | :-- | :--: | :-- |
| **Success Rate (SR)** |   | Higher |   | Fraction meeting the final-position success criterion. |
| **Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE)** |   | Lower |   | Position error over the reference trajectory. |
| **Relative Pose Error (RPE)** |   | Lower |   | Relative translation error between consecutive poses. |
| **Full-route fidelity** |   | Higher |   | Agreement with the complete ordered recorded route, including a penalty for unnecessary travel. |
| **Heading and turn fidelity** |   | Higher |   | Agreement of facing direction while moving and of the direction, position, and amount of turns. |

## Composite Score

Each episode is scored first, then the contributions are averaged:

    Score = (100/N) × Σ_i { FullRouteFidelity_i × (1 + HeadingTurnFidelity_i)/2
                          × [0.70 + 0.10 SR_i + 0.10/(1+ATE_i) + 0.10/(1+RPE_i)] }

SR_i is binary success; ATE_i and RPE_i are per-episode errors in dataset coordinate units. Score averages episode contributions.

Phase 1 ranks by `(Score_val_seen + Score_val_unseen) / 2`, with equal weight for each split. Both split files are required; a submission missing either file is rejected. Both split Scores are displayed. Phase 2 ranks by test Score.
pages.content_zh:
# 提交与评估

将预测的动作序列提交至ZIP压缩包，仅使用每个片段的初始RGB图像和指令。

## 动作格式

每个动作为[dx, dy, dyaw]：前向位移、智能体**当前局部坐标系**中的左向位移，以及偏航角更新（弧度制）。序列长度可不同；JSON列表标记轨迹结束。

限制：每个片段最多64个动作；单次动作的hypot(dx,dy) ≤ 2.46数据集坐标单位且|dyaw| ≤ 6.29弧度（在[−π, π)范围内对2π取模计算）。

## ZIP文件结构

将所需的JSON文件置于压缩包根目录。可下载的示例ZIP展示了文件结构和第一阶段片段ID；替换其中的示例动作。

| 阶段 |   | 所需文件 |
| :-- | :--: | :-- |
| 第一阶段 |   | val_seen.json, val_unseen.json |
| 第二阶段 |   | test.json |

### JSON模式

每个文件包含数据集划分和片段。每个阶段的episode_id必须且只能出现一次，附带动作列表：

    {
      "split": "val_unseen",
      "episodes": [
        {
          "episode_id": "20210826_40_0001_02_0",
          "actions": [[0.25, 0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0, 0.15], [0.12, -0.05, 0.0]]
        }
      ]
    }

此简化示例并非完整提交。

## 评估指标

两个保真度指标范围为0到1。五种计算方法参见[demonstration.py](https://github.com/F1y1113/worldnav-challenge/blob/main/demonstration.py)。

| 指标 |   | 方向 |   | 含义 |
| :-- | :--: | :-- | :--: | :-- |
| **成功率 (SR)** |   | 越高越好 |   | 满足最终位置成功标准的比例。 |
| **绝对轨迹误差 (ATE)** |   | 越低越好 |   | 相对于参考轨迹的位置误差。 |
| **相对位姿误差 (RPE)** |   | 越低越好 |   | 连续位姿之间的相对平移误差。 |
| **全路径保真度** |   | 越高越好 |   | 与完整有序记录路径的一致性，包括对不必要移动的惩罚。 |
| **航向与转向保真度** |   | 越高越好 |   | 移动时朝向以及转向方向、位置和幅度的一致性。 |

## 综合得分

首先对每个片段进行评分，然后取平均值：

    Score = (100/N) × Σ_i { FullRouteFidelity_i × (1 + HeadingTurnFidelity_i)/2
                          × [0.70 + 0.10 SR_i + 0.10/(1+ATE_i) + 0.10/(1+RPE_i)] }

SR_i为二元成功标志；ATE_i和RPE_i为每个片段在数据集坐标单位下的误差。得分取各片段贡献的平均值。

第一阶段按`(Score_val_seen + Score_val_unseen) / 2`排名，两个划分权重相等。两个划分的文件都必须提交；缺少任一文件的提交将被拒绝。两个划分的得分均会显示。第二阶段按测试集得分排名。

pages.title: Overview
pages.content: # Welcome to Track 2: HA-VLN **Human-Aware Vision-and-Language Navigation (HA-VLN)** is Track 2 of [RoboWorld 2026](https://roboworld2026.github.io/), affiliated with the [RoboPAD Workshop at NeurIPS 2026](https://robotpad2026.github.io/). ## Challenge Overview This track challenges participants to develop **human-aware vision-and-language navigation agents** that follow natural-language instructions **safely, efficiently, and socially** in dynamic human environments. While many standard VLN benchmarks assume static scenes, real-world spaces are shared with moving people who serve as both semantic landmarks and dynamic obstacles. Built on [HA-VLN 2.0](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14229), submissions must balance **instruction following** and **social compliance** under partial observability and real-time human interactions. - **Human-Referenced Grounding**: Interpret fine-grained instructions that reference both scene landmarks and ongoing human activities. - **Social Norm Compliance**: Respect personal space, proactively avoid human collisions, and navigate safely around moving bystanders. - **Realistic Benchmarking**: Navigate indoor and outdoor areas with multi-human interactions in the HA-R2R and HAPS 2.0 datasets. We welcome navigation policies, waypoint and topological planners, world models, and VLA approaches that advance safe, human-centered navigation in shared spaces. ## Task Definition - **Input:** A natural-language navigation instruction, initial pose and ongoing agent pose (position and heading from simulator state, GPS+compass), and sequential egocentric forward-facing RGB-D observations. Direct access to ground-truth human trajectories (`human_motion.json`) is strictly prohibited during inference. - **Sensor Setup:** One forward-facing RGB-D camera. Adding additional cameras is not permitted; panoramic views must be acquired by rotating in place (rotation actions count toward the action budget). - **Setting:** **Closed-loop interactive navigation** in continuous 3D environments with dynamic humans. - **Actions:** Six discrete actions: `STOP`, `MOVE_FORWARD`, `TURN_LEFT`, `TURN_RIGHT`, `LOOK_UP`, `LOOK_DOWN`. - **Output:** An ordered sequence of 1 to 500 discrete actions for each episode submitted for official simulator replay. Sequences shorter than 500 actions must end in `STOP`; sequences reaching the 500-action limit may omit `STOP`. - **Objective:** Reach the instructed goal safely while avoiding collisions with humans. ## Phases - Phase 1: Development on released val_seen and val_unseen episodes. Both splits are reported; only the val_unseen Score determines the Phase 1 ranking. - Phase 1 coverage: submit actions for all 778 val_seen episodes and all 1,839 val_unseen episodes. - Phase 2: Final evaluation on withheld test scoring data. The test Score determines final rankings and awards. Phase 1 scores do not determine shortlisting or awards and are not combined with Phase 2 scores. Submit at most five times per day and 100 times per phase; the best Score is retained. ## Schedule 1. Registration opens October 08, 2026. 2. Phase 1 opens October 15, 2026, and closes October 30, 2026. 3. Phase 2 opens October 30, 2026, and closes November 30, 2026. 4. Award decisions are announced on December 12, 2026. ## Awards & Recognition 1. **Certificates of Recognition**: Official certificates awarded to the Top 5 teams in Track 2. 2. **Best Innovative Solution**: Certificate recognizing outstanding creativity and technical innovation. 3. **Oral Presentations**: Selected top-performing teams will be invited to give oral presentations at the RoboPAD Workshop at NeurIPS 2026. Final rankings and awards are determined entirely by Phase 2 test evaluation. ## Materials & Toolkit - [Challenge repository and participant toolkit](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2): Documentation, data download scripts, baseline setup, and action submission exporter. - [Track website](https://roboworld2026.github.io/track2): Official track details and announcements. - [HA-VLN 2.0](https://uwmilab.github.io/HA-VLN-webpage/): Project page and [official repository](https://github.com/UWMILab/HA-VLN). - Starting kit: Download the Phase 1 starting kit attached to this competition for the official episode manifest, example submission, and local validator. ## Registration Register your team through the [Google Form](https://roboworld2026.github.io/#registration) (registration opens October 08, 2026) to be eligible for the leaderboard, certificates, and awards. ## Contact - **Frequently Asked Questions:** [Track 2 FAQ](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2#-frequently-asked-questions) (please check the FAQ before emailing for common questions) - **Technical Support:** [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2/issues) - **Contact Email:** [roboworld2026@gmail.com](mailto:roboworld2026@gmail.com) - **Discord:** [Join the RoboWorld Track 2 Discord](https://discord.gg/S8s8JcxtT) - **WeChat Group:** [Join the RoboWorld Track 2 WeChat Group](https://github.com/roboworld2026/roboworld2026.github.io/blob/main/wechat_track2.JPG)
pages.content_zh:
欢迎来到赛道2：HA-VLN

**具人感知视觉语言导航（HA-VLN）**是 [RoboWorld 2026](https://roboworld2026.github.io/) 的赛道2，隶属于 [NeurIPS 2026 RoboPAD研讨会](https://robotpad2026.github.io/)。

## 挑战赛概述

本赛道要求参赛者开发**具人感知视觉语言导航智能体**，使其能够在动态人体环境中**安全、高效且符合社交规范**地遵循自然语言指令。

尽管许多标准VLN基准测试假设场景是静态的，但真实世界空间与移动的人群共享，这些人既是语义地标也是动态障碍物。基于 [HA-VLN 2.0](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14229)，提交作品必须在部分可观测性和实时人体交互的条件下，平衡**指令遵循**与**社交合规性**。

- **人参考接地**：解读同时参考场景地标和正在进行的人体活动的细粒度指令。
- **社会规范遵守**：尊重个人空间，主动避免与人体碰撞，并安全地绕行移动旁观者。
- **真实基准测试**：在HA-R2R和HAPS 2.0数据集中，在具有多人体交互的室内和室外区域进行导航。

我们欢迎导航策略、路点和拓扑规划器、世界模型以及VLA（视觉语言动作）方法，以推动共享空间中安全、以人为中心的导航技术发展。

## 任务定义

- **输入**：自然语言指令和连续的以自我为中心的RGB-D观测。
- **设置**：在具有动态人体的连续3D环境中进行**闭环交互式导航**。
- **动作**：六个离散动作：`停止`、`前进`、`左转`、`右转`、`抬头`、`低头`。

pages.content:
# Submission & Evaluation

Both phases accept a single ZIP archive containing predicted action sequences for all required episodes.

## What the Submission Contains

Submit one ZIP archive containing action sequences for every episode in the phase manifest. Only action predictions are used for evaluation; model weights, code, and external environment assets are not required.

## Archive Layout

Place the prediction JSON files directly at the root of the ZIP archive:

```text
submission.zip
|-- val_seen.json      # 778 episodes
`-- val_unseen.json    # 1,839 episodes
```

Phase 2 follows the same layout with `test.json` in `submission_test.zip`. Package Phase 1 predictions:

```bash
zip -j submission.zip val_seen.json val_unseen.json
```

## Prediction File Structure

Each JSON file must contain `format_version`, `split`, and `episodes`:

```json
{
  "format_version": 1,
  "split": "val_unseen",
  "episodes": [
    {
      "episode_id": "synthetic-example-001",
      "actions": ["MOVE_FORWARD", "TURN_LEFT", "LOOK_UP", "LOOK_DOWN", "STOP"]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `format_version`: Set to `1`.
- `split`: `"val_seen"`, `"val_unseen"`, or `"test"`, matching the corresponding phase.
- `episodes`: A list of episode predictions covering all episode IDs in the manifest.
  - `episode_id`: String identifier matching the manifest exactly once.
  - `actions`: An ordered list of 1 to 500 actions chosen from `["STOP", "MOVE_FORWARD", "TURN_LEFT", "TURN_RIGHT", "LOOK_UP", "LOOK_DOWN"]`. `"STOP"` may only appear as the final action. Sequences shorter than 500 actions must end with `"STOP"`; sequences reaching the 500-action limit may omit `"STOP"` if terminated by the step limit.

## Evaluation & Leaderboard

Submissions are evaluated on navigation and social compliance, and ranked by the composite challenge **Score** (higher is better):

- **SR** (higher is better): Collision-free navigation success rate to the target goal.
- **NE** (lower is better): Mean Euclidean distance in metres from final agent position to goal.
- **CR** (lower is better): Ratio of collision episodes over human-influenced episodes.
- **TCR** (lower is better): Mean number of collision events per episode.

```text
NE utility  = 3 / (3 + NE)
TCR utility = 1 / (1 + TCR)
Navigation  = 0.80 * SR + 0.20 * NE utility
Social      = 0.75 * (1 - CR) + 0.25 * TCR utility
Score       = 100 * Navigation * (0.70 + 0.30 * Social)
```

Phase 1 ranks teams by `val_unseen` Score (`val_seen` is reported for reference). Phase 2 ranks teams by `test` Score to determine final awards. When Scores are tied, rankings are broken in order: higher SR, lower NE, lower CR, lower TCR, and earlier submission time.

Official evaluation replays submitted action sequences in the organizer-controlled CodaBench environment under standardized conditions. Human animations advance with wall-clock time according to the configured motion FPS (rather than advancing one frame per action). Official CodaBench replay results determine official competition rankings.

## Submission Limits

Each team may submit up to 5 times per day and 100 times per phase. The leaderboard retains the team's highest Score.

## Support

- **Frequently Asked Questions:** [Track 2 FAQ](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2#-frequently-asked-questions) (please check the FAQ before emailing for common questions)
- **Technical Support:** [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2/issues)  
- **Contact Email:** [roboworld2026@gmail.com](mailto:roboworld2026@gmail.com)

提交结果根据导航和社交合规性进行评估，并按综合挑战**分数**进行排名（越高越好）：

- **SR**（越高越好）：到达目标的无碰撞导航成功率。
- **NE**（越低越好）：智能体最终位置到目标的平均欧几里得距离（米）。
- **CR**（越低越好）：碰撞回合与受人类影响回合的比率。
- **TCR**（越低越好）：每回合的平均碰撞事件次数。

```text
NE utility  = 3 / (3 + NE)
TCR utility = 1 / (1 + TCR)
Navigation  = 0.80 * SR + 0.20 * NE utility
Social      = 0.75 * (1 - CR) + 0.25 * TCR utility
Score       = 100 * Navigation * (0.70 + 0.30 * Social)
```

第一阶段根据`val_unseen`分数对队伍进行排名（`val_seen`分数仅供参考）。第二阶段根据`test`分数对队伍进行排名以确定最终奖项。当分数相同时，按以下顺序打破平局：更高的SR、更低的NE、更低的CR、更低的TCR、更早的提交时间。

## 提交限制

每支队伍每天最多可提交5次，每个阶段最多可提交100次。排行榜保留队伍的最高分数。

pages.content:
# LongVQU-Eval Challenge

**Evaluating Long-Term Video Quality Understanding of Large Vision-Language Models**

IEEE Signal Processing Society Challenge 2026

## Motivation

Traditional video quality assessment (VMAF, SSIM, PSNR, NR-VQA models) works well on
short clips but cannot reason over long temporal context and accumulate perceptual
degradations evidence across events.
**LongVQU-Eval Challenge** aims to close this gap with a multiple-choice question-answering assessment built on
[LongVQUBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Aarna004/LongVQUBench). 

## Hierarchical evaluation



| Level | Name                                        | What models must do                                                              |
|:-----:|---------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1     | **LQU** — Local Event Quality Understanding | Detect, localize, classify, and rate the severity of isolated distortion events |
| 2     | **CQR** — Cross-Event Quality Reasoning     | Compare and integrate perceptual evidence across multiple distortion events      |
| 3     | **GQU** — Global Quality Understanding      | Synthesize a holistic quality judgment over the full video                      |



Within each level, questions are further grouped by `qa_category` (e.g. Comparison, Cumulative Effect) and `question_type` (yes-or-no, what, which, how).

## How the challenge works

- **Videos:** Development Phase videos are on
  Hugging Face (`Aarna004/LongVQUBench`, `grouped_tars/<LEVEL>/<Category>/*.tar`);
  Test Phase videos are a separate, currently-unpublished. Please check Data & Submission Format for details.
- **Questions live on Codabench :**  Each phase publishes a `questions.json`
  with the video reference, the question, and its multiple-choice options.
- **Build your model :** Offline (on your own compute)
- **Submit only your predictions :**  CSV format (`question_idx, predicted_option`). 
  See the Data & Submission Format page for the exact format.

Scoring is exact-match accuracy against the hidden ground truth, with no
constraints on your model, framework, or inference setup **(Proprietary,
paid-API-only models are not eligible).**

## Who can participate

Individuals or teams of 1-5. Both academic and industry participants are
welcome.



## Organizers

Arpita Nema (Primary Contact): arpita004@e.ntu.edu.sg

Hanwei Zhu : hanwei.zhu@ntu.edu.sg

Weisi Lin: WSLin@ntu.edu.sg

Nanyang Technological University, Singapore

# LongVQU-Eval 挑战赛

**评估大型视觉语言模型的长期视频质量理解能力**

IEEE信号处理协会挑战赛 2026

## 动机

传统视频质量评估方法（VMAF、SSIM、PSNR、NR-VQA模型）在短视频上表现良好，但无法在长时间上下文上进行推理，也无法跨事件累积感知退化证据。
**LongVQU-Eval挑战赛**旨在通过构建在[LongVQUBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Aarna004/LongVQUBench)基础上的多选问答评估来弥补这一差距。

## 分层评估

| 级别 | 名称 | 模型需要完成的任务 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **LQU** — 局部事件质量理解 | 检测、定位、分类和评定孤立失真事件的严重程度 |
| 2 | **CQR** — 跨事件质量推理 | 比较和整合多个失真事件的感知证据 |
| 3 | **GQU** — 全局质量理解 | 对完整视频进行整体质量判断 |

在每个级别内，问题进一步按`qa_category`（如对比、累积效果）和`question_type`（是/否、什么、哪个、如何）分组。

## 挑战赛运作流程

- **视频：** 开发阶段视频位于Hugging Face（`Aarna004/LongVQUBench`、`grouped_tars/<LEVEL>/<Category>/*.tar`）；测试阶段视频为独立的未公开数据集。请查看数据和提交格式页面了解详情。
- **问题发布在Codabench上：** 每个阶段发布一个`questions.json`文件，包含视频参考、问题和多选选项。
- **构建您的模型：** 离线方式（在您自己的计算环境上）
- **仅提交预测结果：** CSV格式（`question_idx, predicted_option`）。详见数据和提交格式页面的准确格式。

评分为与隐藏真值的完全匹配准确度，对您的模型、框架或推理设置**没有限制**（不允许仅限专有和付费API的模型）。

## 参赛资格

1-5人的个人或团队。欢迎学术和行业参与者。

## 组织者

Arpita Nema（主要联系人）: arpita004@e.ntu.edu.sg

Hanwei Zhu: hanwei.zhu@ntu.edu.sg

Weisi Lin: WSLin@ntu.edu.sg

新加坡南洋理工大学

# Data & Submission Format

## Data Batches

| Batch | Size | Videos | Answers public? | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Development (Train)** | 1,200 MCQs | on Hugging Face now | Yes | Codabench `public_data/train/questions.json` (WITH `answer`/`answer_idx`) |
| **Test** | TBA | TBA | No, until challenge ends | Codabench `public_data/test_public/questions.json` (candidates only) |

These are two **independent** annotation batches with non-overlapping
`question_idx` values. The Train batch's answers are public (it's on the
gated Hugging Face repo, so anyone with Hub access can see them). Please treat
any Dev-phase leaderboard score as your pipeline check. The **Test batch determines the final ranking**.

## Where the data lives

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Train videos | Hugging Face: [`Aarna004/LongVQUBench`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Aarna004/LongVQUBench) — `grouped_tars/<LEVEL>/<Category>/*.tar`. Requires accepting the dataset's terms + a Hub login. |
| Test videos | **TBD** <This row will be replaced with the  link>. |
| Train questions **with answers** | Codabench, Development Phase `public_data/train/questions.json` |
| Test questions **without answers** | Codabench, Test Phase `public_data/test_public/questions.json` |



## `questions.json` schema

One entry per question:

```json
{
  "question_idx": 246,
  "video_idx": 1212,
  "hierarchy_category": "CQR",
  "question_type": "yes-or-no",
  "qa_category": "Comparison",
  "question": "Is the perceptual degradation in the first 30 seconds more severe than that between 138.37s and 153.35s?",
  "candidates": ["Yes", "No"],
  "answer": "No",
  "answer_idx": 2
}
```

- `hierarchy_category`: `"LQU"` | `"CQR"` | `"GQU"`
- `candidates`: 2–4 answer options
- `answer` / `answer_idx`: **present in the Development Phase file only.**
  The Test Phase file omits both — you're scored against a hidden copy.
- `video_idx`: matches the video's identifier inside the Hugging Face
  `grouped_tars` archives — use this to locate the right video.

## What you submit

A single **`predictions.csv`** at the root of your submission zip:

```csv
question_idx,predicted_option
246,4
422,2
469,3
```

`predicted_option` is the **1-based index** into that question's
`candidates` array (e.g. answering `"No"` for
`["Yes", "No"]` → `predicted_option = 2`).



**Unanswered `question_idx` values are scored as incorrect, so partial
submissions are allowed but will lower your accuracy.**

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
# Evaluation

## Metric

**Accuracy**: Exact match between your `predicted_option` and the hidden
`answer_idx`, averaged over all questions in the phase. Unanswered
questions count as incorrect.

The leaderboard also reports accuracy broken out per hierarchy level
(LQU / CQR / GQU) for diagnostic purposes, and the number of questions you
provided an answer for (`# Answered`), but ranking is by **Overall
Accuracy**.

## Leaderboard columns

| Column | Key | Sort |
|---|---|---|
| Overall Accuracy | `accuracy` | desc |
| LQU Accuracy | `lqu_accuracy` | desc |
| CQR Accuracy | `cqr_accuracy` | desc |
| GQU Accuracy | `gqu_accuracy` | desc |
| # Answered | `num_answered` | desc |

Ranking uses `accuracy` as the primary sort key. Ties are broken, in order, by:

1. **Inference time** (lower is better), as reported in the submitted methodology document
2. **Parameter count** (lower is better), as reported in the submitted methodology document

## Submission rule

Each phase uses `Force_Last`: only your most recent successful submission
counts toward your leaderboard position, so resubmitting simply replaces
your prior score rather than stacking multiple ranked entries.

排行榜还报告按层级分类的准确率（LQU / CQR / GQU）用于诊断目的，以及您提供答案的问题数量（`# Answered`），但排名以**整体准确率**为准。

| 整体准确率 | `accuracy` | 降序 |
| LQU准确率 | `lqu_accuracy` | 降序 |

pages.content:
UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge — V2X-Real Track

Update — Due to increased interest from multiple qualified participants, Letters of Intent are now accepted through October 30, 2026, 8:00 PM EDT, aligned with the close of the development phase. Teams that have already submitted an LOI by email need take no further action. Teams joining now can register via our Letter of Intent Form.

Update — the Letter of Intent deadline is extended to August 15, 2026 (previously July 25). All other dates are unchanged.

A track of the 2026 IEEE Big Data Cup, held in conjunction with the IEEE International Conference on Big Data (IEEE BigData) 2026, Phoenix, AZ, USA.

Roadside LiDAR perception for intelligent transportation systems is bottlenecked by the cost and rarity of large, well-annotated real datasets. This challenge asks: can synthetic LiDAR data be made realistic enough that a deep learning model trained on it generalizes to real LiDAR frames?

Towards that, this challenge asks participants to generate their own synthetic LiDAR data targeting the V2X-Real distribution, train an object detector on that data, and submit detections on real held-out frames. We score on (1) how distributionally close their synthetic frames are to real ones, and (2) how well the sim-only detector performs on real frames.

Important Dates

  • Letter of Intent Deadline: August 15, 2026 (extended from July 25)
  • Final Report and Solution Submission Deadline: November 15, 2026
  • Winning Teams Announcement: November 25, 2026
  • Conference: December 14–17, 2026

Reference resources for participants

To support participants who would like a documented starting point, we make publicly available a complete reference pipeline covering synthesis methodology, empirical analysis, ready-to-use synthetic datasets, and an open-source LiDAR data processing and visualization software. These materials are offered as orientation, not as requirements.

The synthesis pipeline is described in UrbanTwin: Building High-Fidelity Digital Twins for Sim2Real LiDAR Perception and Evaluation (arXiv preprint), with a deeper empirical analysis including the distributional realism metrics adopted by this challenge in High-Fidelity Digital Twins for Bridging the Sim2Real Gap in LiDAR-Based ITS Perception (IEEE T-ITS, 2026).

The synthetic LiDAR datasets generated with that pipeline are released in UrbanTwin: Synthetic Roadside LiDAR Datasets (IEEE OJ-ITS, 2026) and are available for download at Harvard Dataverse. Each dataset contains 10K frames annotated across six object categories for detection, tracking, and segmentation tasks, and is directly compatible with the multi-class evaluation used here; empirical analysis in papers include both the distributional realism metrics and single-class 3D object detection study as proof-of-concept. For end-to-end LiDAR processing we also provide our LiGuard Framework (IEEE T-IV, 2026) with short, more software focused read on The Journal of Open Source Software.

What you will do

  1. Download the public real V2X-Real dataset and the released detection-test point clouds (50 real frames, no labels).
  2. Generate synthetic LiDAR frames using any approach you like — simulation (CARLA, LGSVL, custom), generative models (diffusion, GANs, flow-based), hybrid pipelines, or anything else.
  3. Train a 3D object detector (any architecture) on only your synthetic data.
  4. Submit:
    • 50 of your synthetic LiDAR frames,
    • your detector's predictions on the 50 released test point clouds,
    • and a signed honor declaration.

Scoring at a glance

Combined score = 0.6 × normalized 3D mAP + 0.4 × normalized realism, where 3D mAP is averaged across the 3 object categories defined for this track (vehicle, pedestrian, truck) and realism averages normalized Chamfer Distance, MMD, EMD, and Fréchet Point-cloud Distance. See the Evaluation tab for the formulae.

Prizes

Per track:

  • 1st place: USD 500
  • 2nd place: USD 300
  • 3rd place: USD 200

Sponsor(s) will be announced before the Development phase opens.

Phases

  • Development — public leaderboard, up to 5 submissions/day per participant, 100 total. Use this to iterate.
  • Final — private leaderboard until close, 5 total submissions per participant. The final-phase ranking determines the winners.

Baselines

Reference numbers are listed in the Data tab.

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
Evaluation Protocol

Two scores are computed and combined into a single Combined score that determines leaderboard rank.

1. Distributional realism

Aggregation:

  1. Concatenate the 50 submitted synthetic frames into one set S_syn; concatenate the 50 held-out real reference frames into S_real.
  2. Mask both to the point-cloud range [-40, -40, -8, 40, 40, 2].
  3. Subsample uniformly at random to N = 10,000 points per side, with seed 1234 (identical seed used by the local evaluator in the starter kit).
  4. Compute one CD, MMD, EMD, and FPD across the entire 10,000-point sets.

1a. Chamfer Distance (CD)

CD(P, Q) = (1/|P|) Σ_{p ∈ P} min_{q ∈ Q} ||p - q||²
         + (1/|Q|) Σ_{q ∈ Q} min_{p ∈ P} ||p - q||²

Squared-L2 nearest-neighbor cost; symmetric. Lower is better.

1b. Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD)

MMD²(X, Y) = E[k(x, x')] + E[k(y, y')] - 2 E[k(x, y)],   k(a, b) = exp(-γ ||a - b||²)

Unbiased estimator (off-diagonal). Bandwidth γ is set by the median heuristic on a 1 000-point joint subsample (γ = 1 / (2 · median ||x - y||²)) so the kernel does not saturate at LiDAR spatial scales. Lower is better.

1c. Earth Mover's Distance (EMD)

EMD(X, Y) = √ ( min_{T ∈ Π(X, Y)} Σ_{i,j} T_{ij} · ||x_i - y_j|| )

Wasserstein-1 with Euclidean ground cost, solved exactly by the network simplex (POT's ot.emd2). Reported in metres. Lower is better.

1d. Fréchet Point-cloud Distance (FPD)

FPD = ||μ_X - μ_Y||² + Tr(Σ_X + Σ_Y - 2 (Σ_X · Σ_Y)^{1/2})

FID-style: fits a 3-variate Gaussian to each set's points, computes the 2-Wasserstein between Gaussians. Lower is better.

2. 3D Object Detection

Participants submit detections (predictions.json) on 50 real LiDAR frames whose ground truth is held out. We compute average precision over the 3 object categories defined for this track (vehicle, pedestrian, truck), at IoU thresholds 0.5 (primary) and 0.7 (secondary). Per-class AP is reported, and mean AP across classes (mAP) is the leaderboard's detection score; classes with zero ground-truth instances in the held-out set are excluded from the mean. Both KITTI 11-point and 40-point interpolated AP are reported; the 40-point form is the leaderboard primary.

Ground-truth and predicted boxes use the OpenPCDet 7-DoF format [x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading]. IoU is computed as 3D intersection-over-union between two oriented BEV rectangles times the Z overlap. The KITTI truncation/occlusion/min-height difficulty filter is not applied because those depend on 2D bounding-box annotations that are not natural for roadside LiDAR datasets.

The valid class strings for this track are listed in config.json (shipped in reference_data/) and in submission_format.md in the starter kit. Any prediction with an unrecognized class label is discarded.

3. Combined score

Each component is min-max normalized into [0, 1] using a per-track normalization range:

score_realism   = mean( norm(CD), norm(MMD), norm(EMD), norm(FPD) )    (lower-is-better → 1 - clip)
score_detection = norm( AP_3d @ IoU 0.5 )                               (higher-is-better → clip)
score_combined  = 0.6 · score_detection + 0.4 · score_realism

Normalization endpoints are public in config.json (shipped in reference_data/), so the local evaluator and the server compute identical scores.

Reproducibility

  • Realism is dataset-level — frame ordering does not matter. Submit the 50 synthetic frames in any consistent naming.
  • Subsampling RNG seed: 1234 (same on server and starting kit).
  • The exact scoring program shipped to the Codabench worker is included in the starting kit.
pages.content_zh:
评估协议

计算两个分数并合并为单一的综合分数，以决定排行榜排名。

1. 分布真实性

聚合：

  1. 将50帧提交的合成帧拼接为一个集合S_syn；将50帧留出的真实参考帧拼接为S_real。
  2. 将两者掩膜至点云范围[-40, -40, -8, 40, 40, 2]。
  3. 使用随机均匀子采样，每侧N = 10,000个点，随机种子为1234（与入门套件中本地评估器使用的种子相同）。
  4. 在整个10,000点集合上计算一个CD、MMD、EMD和FPD。

1a. 倒角距离（CD）

CD(P, Q) = (1/|P|) Σ_{p ∈ P} min_{q ∈ Q} ||p - q||²
         + (1/|Q|) Σ_{q ∈ Q} min_{p ∈ P} ||p - q||²

平方L2最近邻代价；对称。越低越好。

1b. 最大均值差异（MMD）

MMD²(X, Y) = E[k(x, x')] + E[k(y, y')] - 2 E[k(x, y)],   k(a, b) = exp(-γ ||a - b||²)

无偏估计量（非对角线）。带宽γ通过在1,000点联合子样本上的中位数启发式设置（γ = 1 / (2 · median ||x - y||²)），以确保核函数在LiDAR空间尺度上不饱和。越低越好。

1c. 推土机距离（EMD）

EMD(X, Y) = √ ( min_{T ∈ Π(X, Y)} Σ_{i,j} T_{ij} · ||x_i - y_j|| )

具有欧几里得地面代价的Wasserstein-1距离，通过网络单纯形法（POT的ot.emd2）精确求解。以米为单位报告。越低越好。

1d. 弗雷歇点云距离（FPD）

FPD = ||μ_X - μ_Y||² + Tr(Σ_X + Σ_Y - 2 (Σ_X · Σ_Y)^{1/2})

FID风格：将三变量高斯分布拟合到每个集合的点，计算高斯分布之间的2-Wasserstein距离。越低越好。

2. 3D目标检测

参与者提交在50帧真实LiDAR帧上的检测结果（predictions.json），这些帧的真实标注被保留。我们在本赛道定义的3个目标类别（车辆、行人、卡车）上计算平均精度，IoU阈值分别为0.5（主要）和0.7（次要）。报告每类AP，跨类别平均AP（mAP）作为排行榜的检测分数；在留出集中真实实例为零的类别不参与平均。同时报告KITTI 11点和40点插值AP；40点形式为排行榜主要指标。

真实标注和预测框使用OpenPCDet 7自由度格式[x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading]。IoU计算为两个定向BEV矩形之间的3D交并比乘以Z轴重叠率。不应用KITTI截断/遮挡/最小高度难度过滤，因为这些依赖于2D边界框标注，而这对于路边LiDAR数据集并不自然。

本赛道有效的类别字符串列于config.json（随reference_data/提供）和入门套件中的submission_format.md。任何具有无法识别类别标签的预测将被丢弃。

3. 综合分数

每个组件使用每个赛道的归一化范围进行最小-最大归一化至[0, 1]：

score_realism   = mean( norm(CD), norm(MMD), norm(EMD), norm(FPD) )    （越低越好 → 1 - clip）
score_detection = norm( AP_3d @ IoU 0.5 )                               （越高越好 → clip）
score_combined  = 0.6 · score_detection + 0.4 · score_realism

归一化端点公开于config.json（随reference_data/提供），因此本地评估器和服务器计算相同的分数。

pages.title: Data
pages.content:
Data

V2X-Real

Real V2X-Real data is publicly available from its original release. We do not redistribute it. Participants must obtain the real dataset directly from its source under its own license.

  • Source: https://github.com/ucla-mobility/V2X-Real
  • License: see the source.

Released for participants

The starting kit (Files tab → starting_kit) contains:

  • detection_test_frames/ — 50 real LiDAR frames (point clouds only, no labels) on which you must run your detector and submit predictions.
  • detection_test_frame_ids.json — the canonical list of frame IDs your predictions.json must cover, in order.
  • forbidden_frames.txt — 100 frame IDs you may not train, validate, or hyperparameter-tune on. This is the union of the 50 detection-test frames and the 50 realism-reference frames. Honor system, enforced by signed declaration in your submission.
  • local_eval.py — the exact scoring program shipped to the Codabench worker. Run it locally to reproduce server scores bit-for-bit, given a dummy reference set you generate from the released detection-test frames.
  • make_dummy_submission.py — produces a known-bad submission that exercises the format. Useful for sanity-checking your pipeline.
  • submission_format.md — full submission spec.

Held out (organizer-only)

  • 50 real frames used as the realism reference set.
  • Ground-truth boxes for the 50 detection-test frames.

Categories evaluated

This track is scored on 3 object categories defined for the V2X-Real dataset: vehicle, pedestrian, truck. The leaderboard's detection score is the mean AP across these categories; classes with zero ground-truth instances in the held-out 50-frame set are excluded from the mean.

Splits

Splits are stratified random samples with fixed seed 1234. The exact frame ID lists are published in the starting kit so anyone can reproduce them from the released real dataset.

Reference baselines

The numbers below are reported for the Car class only, taken from prior work on this dataset. The leaderboard's detection score is the mean AP across all categories defined for this track (see Evaluation), so submissions are scored on broader coverage than these single-class references. The baselines are included to demonstrate that sim → real transfer is achievable on this benchmark and to provide a per-class reference point for orientation while you iterate.

SystemCar 3D AP @ 0.5Car 3D AP @ 0.7
V2X-Real no-fusion benchmark (SECOND, real) 0.3556 n/r
SECOND (UT-V2X-Real synthetic → V2X-Real-IC, IEEE T-ITS 2026) 0.6318 n/r

  • make_dummy_submission.py — 生成一个已知错误的提交以测试格式。可用于对您的流程进行合理性检查。
  • submission_format.md — 完整提交规范。

保留数据（仅组织者可见）

  • 50帧用作真实性参考集的真实数据。
  • 50个检测测试帧的真值框。

评估类别

本赛道基于为V2X-Real数据集定义的3个目标类别进行评分： 车辆、行人、卡车。排行榜的检测分数为这些类别的平均AP；在保留的50帧数据集中真值实例数为零的类别不纳入平均值计算。

数据划分

划分采用固定随机种子1234的分层随机抽样。精确的帧ID列表已发布在启动工具包中，任何人都可以从发布的真实数据集中复现这些划分。

参考基线

以下数值仅针对车辆类别报告，引用自此数据集上的已有研究。排行榜的检测分数为本赛道定义的所有类别的平均AP（参见评估部分），因此提交作品将在比这些单类别参考更广的覆盖范围上评分。纳入这些基线是为了证明在此基准上仿真到真实的迁移是可行的，并在您迭代过程中提供逐类别的参考点。

pages.title: Submission
pages.content:
Submission Format

Pack everything below into a single submission.zip and upload it on the Submit tab.

submission.zip
├── synthetic/
│   ├── 0001.bin
│   ├── 0002.bin
│   ├── ...
│   └── 0050.bin           # exactly 50 files
├── predictions.json
└── declaration.pdf        # signed honor declaration (PDF). declaration.txt also accepted.

synthetic/<id>.bin

  • Exactly 50 files.
  • Each file is raw float32, shape N × 3, in row-major order, with channels (x, y, z) in metres.
  • Either N × 3 or N × 4 (xyz + intensity) is accepted; the intensity column, if present, is dropped before scoring.
  • Each file ≤ 1.5 MB on disk (~125,000 points). Realism is computed at the dataset level: all 50 frames are concatenated, masked to the track's point-cloud range, then subsampled to 10,000 points (seed 1234) before computing CD / MMD / EMD / FPD. Submitting denser frames does not improve scores; frame ordering does not matter.
  • The simplest valid naming is 0001.bin … 0050.bin.

predictions.json

JSON object whose keys are the frame IDs from detection_test_frame_ids.json (in the starting kit). For every frame ID you must include an entry, even if the value is an empty list.

{
  "<frame_id_1>": [
    {"box": [x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading], "score": 0.97, "class": "vehicle"},
    {"box": [...],                          "score": 0.81, "class": "pedestrian"}
  ],
  "<frame_id_2>": [],
  ...
}
  • box: 7 floats, OpenPCDet convention. (x, y, z) is the box center in metres in the LiDAR frame, (dx, dy, dz) are full extents along the box-local axes, heading is rotation around +Z in radians.
  • score: confidence in [0, 1].
  • class: one of the valid class strings for this track. Valid values: vehicle, pedestrian, truck. Class strings are matched case-insensitively. Predictions with unrecognized class strings are discarded before AP is computed.

declaration.pdf (or declaration.txt)

The starter kit ships declaration_template.pdf, a one-page form with the required honor statement preprinted and a signature line. Fill in team name and date, sign (digitally with any PDF tool, or print → sign → scan), save as declaration.pdf, and include it in every submission.

If you cannot easily produce a signed PDF, a plain declaration.txt is also accepted. Required statement (verbatim, case-insensitive):

I confirm that I did not train on any frame listed in forbidden_frames.txt, and that all submitted detections were produced by a model trained only on synthetic data I generated.

What gets returned

After scoring (typically < 5 minutes for valid submissions) you'll see your position on the leaderboard plus a Detailed Results view with all component metrics, including per-class AP.

提交格式

将所有以下内容打包到一个 submission.zip 文件中，并在提交标签页上传。

submission.zip
├── synthetic/
│   ├── 0001.bin
│   ├── 0002.bin
│   ├── ...
│   └── 0050.bin           # 恰好 50 个文件
├── predictions.json
└── declaration.pdf        # 签署的诚信声明（PDF）。也接受 declaration.txt。

synthetic/<id>.bin

  • 恰好 50 个文件。
  • 每个文件为原始 float32 格式，形状为 N × 3，按行优先顺序排列，通道为 (x, y, z)，单位为米。
  • 接受 N × 3 或 N × 4（xyz + 强度）格式；如果存在强度列，将在评分前被丢弃。
  • 每个文件在磁盘上不超过 1.5 MB（约 125,000 个点）。真实感在数据集层面计算：所有 50 帧被拼接，根据赛道的点云范围进行掩码处理，然后下采样至 10,000 个点（随机种子 1234），再计算 CD / MMD / EMD / FPD。提交更密集的帧不会提高分数；帧顺序无关紧要。
  • 最简单的有效命名方式为 0001.bin … 0050.bin。

predictions.json

JSON 对象的键为 detection_test_frame_ids.json（在起始套件中）中的帧 ID。对于每个帧 ID，您都必须包含一个条目，即使该值为空列表。

{
  "<frame_id_1>": [
    {"box": [x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading], "score": 0.97, "class": "vehicle"},
    {"box": [...],                          "score": 0.81, "class": "pedestrian"}
  ],
  "<frame_id_2>": [],
  ...
}
  • box：7 个浮点数，遵循 OpenPCDet 约定。(x, y, z) 是 LiDAR 坐标系中包围框中心的坐标（单位：米），(dx, dy, dz) 是沿包围框局部坐标轴的全尺寸，heading 是绕 +Z 轴的旋转角度（单位：弧度）。
  • score：置信度，范围为 [0, 1]。
  • class：该赛道的有效类别字符串之一。有效值：vehicle、pedestrian、truck。类别字符串匹配时不区分大小写。在计算 AP 之前，类别字符串无法识别的预测将被丢弃。

declaration.pdf（或 declaration.txt）

起始套件包含 declaration_template.pdf，这是一份单页表格，预先印有所需的诚信声明和签名栏。填写团队名称和日期，签名（使用任意 PDF 工具进行数字签名，或打印 → 签名 → 扫描），保存为 declaration.pdf，并包含在每次提交中。

如果您无法方便地生成签名 PDF，也接受纯文本 declaration.txt。所需声明（逐字，不区分大小写）：

我确认我未使用 forbidden_frames.txt 中列出的任何帧进行训练，且所有提交的检测结果均由仅使用我生成的合成数据训练的模型产生。

返回结果

评分后（有效提交通常少于 5 分钟），您将看到自己在排行榜上的位置，以及包含所有组件指标（包括每类 AP）的详细结果视图。

pages.title: Rules
pages.content:
Rules

Eligibility

  • Open to anyone — researchers, students, industry teams.
  • Each team must register one participant account; do not maintain multiple accounts.

Allowed

  • Any simulation framework or generative model (CARLA, Helios++, OpenScene, neural radiance fields, diffusion, GANs, custom physics). Open or closed source — what matters is the synthesized data.
  • Any 3D object detector architecture, trained on your synthetic data only.
  • Augmentations applied during detector training (rotation, scale, flip, ground-truth sampling, noise) — they operate on synthetic data, not on the forbidden real frames.
  • Using the train split of the public real dataset for hyperparameter selection or domain adaptation, provided no forbidden frame is touched. (The forbidden list contains only the 100 reserved frames, not the entire real train split.)

Forbidden

  • Training, validating, hyperparameter-tuning, or otherwise observing ground truth from any of the 100 frames listed in forbidden_frames.txt. This is enforced by signed declaration and is the foundational integrity rule of the challenge.
  • Submitting predictions produced by a model that has been trained on real labels for any roadside-LiDAR dataset. The detector must be sim-only.
  • Reverse-engineering or inferring the held-out realism reference frames via Codabench's leaderboard signal (e.g., probing submissions designed to leak the reference set's identity). Submissions found to be doing this will be disqualified.
  • Multiple accounts, sub-team accounts, or coordinating across registered teams.

Disqualification

Organizers reserve the right to inspect the synthetic frames and predictions of any submission for evidence of forbidden-frame leakage (e.g., synthetic frames that suspiciously resemble held-out real frames; predictions whose distribution implies access to held-out ground truth). Disqualified participants are removed from the leaderboard and from prize consideration.

Prizes

Per track: 1st place USD 500, 2nd place USD 300, 3rd place USD 200. Sponsor(s) will be announced before the Development phase opens.

Publication and credit

  • Every participating team submits a 4–8 page challenge report describing their approach, due by the final-phase deadline (November 15, 2026).
  • Teams that prefer not to publish may opt into the non-publication track for their submission.
  • Top-3 teams per track are invited to present at the IEEE BigData 2026 Big Data Cup workshop session in Phoenix, AZ (December 14–17, 2026), and to submit a full paper to the IEEE BigData 2026 proceedings through the challenge's associated paper track.
  • The challenge organizers may publish an aggregate analysis of all submissions (anonymized unless explicit permission is granted).

规则

参赛资格

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge — LUMPI Track

Update — Due to increased interest from multiple qualified participants, Letters of Intent are now accepted through October 30, 2026, 8:00 PM EDT, aligned with the close of the development phase. Teams that have already submitted an LOI by email need take no further action. Teams joining now can register via our Letter of Intent Form.

Update — the Letter of Intent deadline is extended to August 15, 2026 (previously July 25). All other dates are unchanged.

A track of the 2026 IEEE Big Data Cup, held in conjunction with the IEEE International Conference on Big Data (IEEE BigData) 2026, Phoenix, AZ, USA.

Roadside LiDAR perception for intelligent transportation systems is bottlenecked by the cost and rarity of large, well-annotated real datasets. This challenge asks: can synthetic LiDAR data be made realistic enough that a deep learning model trained on it generalizes to real LiDAR frames?

Towards that, this challenge asks participants to generate their own synthetic LiDAR data targeting the LUMPI distribution, train an object detector on that data, and submit detections on real held-out frames. We score on (1) how distributionally close their synthetic frames are to real ones, and (2) how well the sim-only detector performs on real frames.

Important Dates

  • Letter of Intent Deadline: August 15, 2026 (extended from July 25)
  • Final Report and Solution Submission Deadline: November 15, 2026
  • Winning Teams Announcement: November 25, 2026
  • Conference: December 14–17, 2026

Reference resources for participants

To support participants who would like a documented starting point, we make publicly available a complete reference pipeline covering synthesis methodology, empirical analysis, ready-to-use synthetic datasets, and an open-source LiDAR data processing and visualization software. These materials are offered as orientation, not as requirements.

The synthesis pipeline is described in UrbanTwin: Building High-Fidelity Digital Twins for Sim2Real LiDAR Perception and Evaluation (arXiv preprint), with a deeper empirical analysis including the distributional realism metrics adopted by this challenge in High-Fidelity Digital Twins for Bridging the Sim2Real Gap in LiDAR-Based ITS Perception (IEEE T-ITS, 2026).

The synthetic LiDAR datasets generated with that pipeline are released in UrbanTwin: Synthetic Roadside LiDAR Datasets (IEEE OJ-ITS, 2026) and are available for download at Harvard Dataverse. Each dataset contains 10K frames annotated across six object categories for detection, tracking, and segmentation tasks, and is directly compatible with the multi-class evaluation used here; empirical analysis in papers include both the distributional realism metrics and single-class 3D object detection study as proof-of-concept. For end-to-end LiDAR processing we also provide our LiGuard Framework (IEEE T-IV, 2026) with short, more software focused read on The Journal of Open Source Software.

What you will do

  1. Download the public real LUMPI dataset and the released detection-test point clouds (50 real frames, no labels).
  2. Generate synthetic LiDAR frames using any approach you like — simulation (CARLA, LGSVL, custom), generative models (diffusion, GANs, flow-based), hybrid pipelines, or anything else.
  3. Train a 3D object detector (any architecture) on only your synthetic data.
  4. Submit:
    • 50 of your synthetic LiDAR frames,
    • your detector's predictions on the 50 released test point clouds,
    • and a signed honor declaration.

Scoring at a glance

Combined score = 0.6 × normalized 3D mAP + 0.4 × normalized realism, where 3D mAP is averaged across the 8 object categories defined for this track (Person, Car, Bicycle, Motorcycle, Bus, Truck, Van, Unknown) and realism averages normalized Chamfer Distance, MMD, EMD, and Fréchet Point-cloud Distance. See the Evaluation tab for the formulae.

Prizes

Per track:

  • 1st place: USD 500
  • 2nd place: USD 300
  • 3rd place: USD 200

Sponsor(s) will be announced before the Development phase opens.

Phases

  • Development — public leaderboard, up to 5 submissions/day per participant, 100 total. Use this to iterate.
  • Final — private leaderboard until close, 5 total submissions per participant. The final-phase ranking determines the winners.

Baselines

Reference numbers are listed in the Data tab.
pages.content_zh:
UrbanTwin 仿真到真实激光雷达挑战赛 — LUMPI 赛道

更新 — 由于众多符合条件的参与者兴趣增加，意向书现接受提交的截止日期延长至2026年10月30日晚8:00（美国东部时间），与开发阶段结束时间一致。已通过电子邮件提交意向书的团队无需进一步操作。现在加入的团队可通过我们的意向书表格注册。

更新 — 意向书截止日期延长至2026年8月15日 （此前为7月25日）。其他所有日期保持不变。

2026年IEEE大数据杯的赛道之一，与2026年IEEE大数据国际会议（IEEE BigData 2026）同期举行，地点：美国亚利桑那州凤凰城。

路侧激光雷达感知在智能交通系统中的发展受限于大规模、高质量标注的真实数据集的成本高昂和稀缺性。本挑战赛提出疑问：合成激光雷达数据能否做到足够真实，使得在其上训练的深度学习模型能够泛化到真实激光雷达帧？

为此，本挑战赛要求参与者生成针对LUMPI分布的合成激光雷达数据，在该数据上训练目标检测器，并对真实的留测试帧提交检测结果。我们将从以下两方面评分：(1) 其合成帧与真实帧的分布接近程度，(2) 纯仿真训练的检测器在真实帧上的表现。

重要日期

参赛者参考资料

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
Evaluation Protocol

Two scores are computed and combined into a single Combined score that determines leaderboard rank.

1. Distributional realism

Aggregation:

  1. Concatenate the 50 submitted synthetic frames into one set S_syn; concatenate the 50 held-out real reference frames into S_real.
  2. Mask both to the point-cloud range [-40, -40, -5, 40, 40, 5].
  3. Subsample uniformly at random to N = 10,000 points per side, with seed 1234 (identical seed used by the local evaluator in the starter kit).
  4. Compute one CD, MMD, EMD, and FPD across the entire 10,000-point sets.

1a. Chamfer Distance (CD)

CD(P, Q) = (1/|P|) Σ_{p ∈ P} min_{q ∈ Q} ||p - q||²
         + (1/|Q|) Σ_{q ∈ Q} min_{p ∈ P} ||p - q||²

Squared-L2 nearest-neighbor cost; symmetric. Lower is better.

1b. Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD)

MMD²(X, Y) = E[k(x, x')] + E[k(y, y')] - 2 E[k(x, y)],   k(a, b) = exp(-γ ||a - b||²)

Unbiased estimator (off-diagonal). Bandwidth γ is set by the median heuristic on a 1 000-point joint subsample (γ = 1 / (2 · median ||x - y||²)) so the kernel does not saturate at LiDAR spatial scales. Lower is better.

1c. Earth Mover's Distance (EMD)

EMD(X, Y) = √ ( min_{T ∈ Π(X, Y)} Σ_{i,j} T_{ij} · ||x_i - y_j|| )

Wasserstein-1 with Euclidean ground cost, solved exactly by the network simplex (POT's ot.emd2). Reported in metres. Lower is better.

1d. Fréchet Point-cloud Distance (FPD)

FPD = ||μ_X - μ_Y||² + Tr(Σ_X + Σ_Y - 2 (Σ_X · Σ_Y)^{1/2})

FID-style: fits a 3-variate Gaussian to each set's points, computes the 2-Wasserstein between Gaussians. Lower is better.

2. 3D Object Detection

Participants submit detections (predictions.json) on 50 real LiDAR frames whose ground truth is held out. We compute average precision over the 8 object categories defined for this track (Person, Car, Bicycle, Motorcycle, Bus, Truck, Van, Unknown), at IoU thresholds 0.5 (primary) and 0.7 (secondary). Per-class AP is reported, and mean AP across classes (mAP) is the leaderboard's detection score; classes with zero ground-truth instances in the held-out set are excluded from the mean. Both KITTI 11-point and 40-point interpolated AP are reported; the 40-point form is the leaderboard primary.

Ground-truth and predicted boxes use the OpenPCDet 7-DoF format [x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading]. IoU is computed as 3D intersection-over-union between two oriented BEV rectangles times the Z overlap. The KITTI truncation/occlusion/min-height difficulty filter is not applied because those depend on 2D bounding-box annotations that are not natural for roadside LiDAR datasets.

The valid class strings for this track are listed in config.json (shipped in reference_data/) and in submission_format.md in the starter kit. Any prediction with an unrecognized class label is discarded.

3. Combined score

Each component is min-max normalized into [0, 1] using a per-track normalization range:

score_realism   = mean( norm(CD), norm(MMD), norm(EMD), norm(FPD) )    (lower-is-better → 1 - clip)
score_detection = norm( AP_3d @ IoU 0.5 )                               (higher-is-better → clip)
score_combined  = 0.6 · score_detection + 0.4 · score_realism

Normalization endpoints are public in config.json (shipped in reference_data/), so the local evaluator and the server compute identical scores.

Reproducibility

  • Realism is dataset-level — frame ordering does not matter. Submit the 50 synthetic frames in any consistent naming.
  • Subsampling RNG seed: 1234 (same on server and starting kit).
  • The exact scoring program shipped to the Codabench worker is included in the starting kit.
pages.content_zh:
评估协议

计算两个分数并合并为一个综合分数，该分数决定排行榜排名。

1. 分布真实性

聚合：

  1. 将50个提交的合成帧拼接为一个集合S_syn；将50个留出的真实参考帧拼接为S_real。
  2. 将两者裁剪至点云范围[-40, -40, -5, 40, 40, 5]。
  3. 使用随机种子1234（与入门套件中本地评估器使用的种子相同），在每侧均匀随机子采样至N = 10,000个点。
  4. 在整个10,000点集合上计算一个CD、MMD、EMD和FPD。

1a. Chamfer距离（CD）

CD(P, Q) = (1/|P|) Σ_{p ∈ P} min_{q ∈ Q} ||p - q||²
         + (1/|Q|) Σ_{q ∈ Q} min_{p ∈ P} ||p - q||²

平方L2最近邻代价；对称。越低越好。

1b. 最大均值差异（MMD）

MMD²(X, Y) = E[k(x, x')] + E[k(y, y')] - 2 E[k(x, y)],   k(a, b) = exp(-γ ||a - b||²)

无偏估计量（非对角线）。带宽γ通过1,000点联合子样本的中位数启发式方法设置（γ = 1 / (2 · 中位数 ||x - y||²)），以使核函数在激光雷达空间尺度上不会饱和。越低越好。

1c. 推土机距离（EMD）

EMD(X, Y) = √ ( min_{T ∈ Π(X, Y)} Σ_{i,j} T_{ij} · ||x_i - y_j|| )

使用欧几里得地面成本的Wasserstein-1距离，通过网络单纯形法（POT的ot.emd2）精确求解。以米为单位报告。越低越好。

1d. Fréchet点云距离（FPD）

FPD = ||μ_X - μ_Y||²

Data

LUMPI

Real LUMPI data is publicly available from its original release. We do not redistribute it. Participants must obtain the real dataset directly from its source under its own license.

  • Source: https://data.uni-hannover.de/dataset/lumpi
  • License: see the source.

Released for participants

The starting kit (Files tab → starting_kit) contains:

  • detection_test_frames/ — 50 real LiDAR frames (point clouds only, no labels) on which you must run your detector and submit predictions.
  • detection_test_frame_ids.json — the canonical list of frame IDs your predictions.json must cover, in order.
  • forbidden_frames.txt — 100 frame IDs you may not train, validate, or hyperparameter-tune on. This is the union of the 50 detection-test frames and the 50 realism-reference frames. Honor system, enforced by signed declaration in your submission.
  • local_eval.py — the exact scoring program shipped to the Codabench worker. Run it locally to reproduce server scores bit-for-bit, given a dummy reference set you generate from the released detection-test frames.
  • make_dummy_submission.py — produces a known-bad submission that exercises the format. Useful for sanity-checking your pipeline.
  • submission_format.md — full submission spec.

Held out (organizer-only)

  • 50 real frames used as the realism reference set.
  • Ground-truth boxes for the 50 detection-test frames.

Categories evaluated

This track is scored on 8 object categories defined for the LUMPI dataset: Person, Car, Bicycle, Motorcycle, Bus, Truck, Van, Unknown. The leaderboard's detection score is the mean AP across these categories; classes with zero ground-truth instances in the held-out 50-frame set are excluded from the mean.

Splits

Splits are stratified random samples with fixed seed 1234. The exact frame ID lists are published in the starting kit so anyone can reproduce them from the released real dataset.

Reference baselines

The numbers below are reported for the Car class only, taken from prior work on this dataset. The leaderboard's detection score is the mean AP across all categories defined for this track (see Evaluation), so submissions are scored on broader coverage than these single-class references. The baselines are included to demonstrate that sim → real transfer is achievable on this benchmark and to provide a per-class reference point for orientation while you iterate.

pages.title: Submission
pages.content:
Submission Format

Pack everything below into a single submission.zip and upload it on the Submit tab.

submission.zip
├── synthetic/
│   ├── 0001.bin
│   ├── 0002.bin
│   ├── ...
│   └── 0050.bin           # exactly 50 files
├── predictions.json
└── declaration.pdf        # signed honor declaration (PDF). declaration.txt also accepted.

synthetic/<id>.bin

  • Exactly 50 files.
  • Each file is raw float32, shape N × 3, in row-major order, with channels (x, y, z) in metres.
  • Either N × 3 or N × 4 (xyz + intensity) is accepted; the intensity column, if present, is dropped before scoring.
  • Each file ≤ 1.5 MB on disk (~125,000 points). Realism is computed at the dataset level: all 50 frames are concatenated, masked to the track's point-cloud range, then subsampled to 10,000 points (seed 1234) before computing CD / MMD / EMD / FPD. Submitting denser frames does not improve scores; frame ordering does not matter.
  • The simplest valid naming is 0001.bin … 0050.bin.

predictions.json

JSON object whose keys are the frame IDs from detection_test_frame_ids.json (in the starting kit). For every frame ID you must include an entry, even if the value is an empty list.

{
  "<frame_id_1>": [
    {"box": [x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading], "score": 0.97, "class": "Car"},
    {"box": [...],                          "score": 0.81, "class": "Person"}
  ],
  "<frame_id_2>": [],
  ...
}
  • box: 7 floats, OpenPCDet convention. (x, y, z) is the box center in metres in the LiDAR frame, (dx, dy, dz) are full extents along the box-local axes, heading is rotation around +Z in radians.
  • score: confidence in [0, 1].
  • class: one of the valid class strings for this track. Valid values: Person, Car, Bicycle, Motorcycle, Bus, Truck, Van, Unknown. Class strings are matched case-insensitively. Predictions with unrecognized class strings are discarded before AP is computed.

declaration.pdf (or declaration.txt)

The starter kit ships declaration_template.pdf, a one-page form with the required honor statement preprinted and a signature line. Fill in team name and date, sign (digitally with any PDF tool, or print → sign → scan), save as declaration.pdf, and include it in every submission.

If you cannot easily produce a signed PDF, a plain declaration.txt is also accepted. Required statement (verbatim, case-insensitive):

I confirm that I did not train on any frame listed in forbidden_frames.txt, and that all submitted detections were produced by a model trained only on synthetic data I generated.

What gets returned

After scoring (typically < 5 minutes for valid submissions) you'll see your position on the leaderboard plus a Detailed Results view with all component metrics, including per-class AP.

返回内容

评分后（有效提交通常少于5分钟），您将看到自己在排行榜上的位置，以及包含所有分项指标（包括每类AP）的详细结果视图。

pages.title: Rules
pages.content:
Rules

Eligibility

  • Open to anyone — researchers, students, industry teams.
  • Each team must register one participant account; do not maintain multiple accounts.

Allowed

  • Any simulation framework or generative model (CARLA, Helios++, OpenScene, neural radiance fields, diffusion, GANs, custom physics). Open or closed source — what matters is the synthesized data.
  • Any 3D object detector architecture, trained on your synthetic data only.
  • Augmentations applied during detector training (rotation, scale, flip, ground-truth sampling, noise) — they operate on synthetic data, not on the forbidden real frames.
  • Using the train split of the public real dataset for hyperparameter selection or domain adaptation, provided no forbidden frame is touched. (The forbidden list contains only the 100 reserved frames, not the entire real train split.)

Forbidden

  • Training, validating, hyperparameter-tuning, or otherwise observing ground truth from any of the 100 frames listed in forbidden_frames.txt. This is enforced by signed declaration and is the foundational integrity rule of the challenge.
  • Submitting predictions produced by a model that has been trained on real labels for any roadside-LiDAR dataset. The detector must be sim-only.
  • Reverse-engineering or inferring the held-out realism reference frames via Codabench's leaderboard signal (e.g., probing submissions designed to leak the reference set's identity). Submissions found to be doing this will be disqualified.
  • Multiple accounts, sub-team accounts, or coordinating across registered teams.

Disqualification

Organizers reserve the right to inspect the synthetic frames and predictions of any submission for evidence of forbidden-frame leakage (e.g., synthetic frames that suspiciously resemble held-out real frames; predictions whose distribution implies access to held-out ground truth). Disqualified participants are removed from the leaderboard and from prize consideration.

Prizes

Per track: 1st place USD 500, 2nd place USD 300, 3rd place USD 200. Sponsor(s) will be announced before the Development phase opens.

Publication and credit

  • Every participating team submits a 4–8 page challenge report describing their approach, due by the final-phase deadline (November 15, 2026).
  • Teams that prefer not to publish may opt into the non-publication track for their submission.
  • Top-3 teams per track are invited to present at the IEEE BigData 2026 Big Data Cup workshop session in Phoenix, AZ (December 14–17, 2026), and to submit a full paper to the IEEE BigData 2026 proceedings through the challenge's associated paper track.
  • The challenge organizers may publish an aggregate analysis of all submissions (anonymized unless explicit permission is granted).

规则

参赛资格

  • 面向所有人员开放 — 研究人员、学生、行业团队。
  • 每支团队必须注册一个参赛账号；请勿维护多个账号。

允许事项

  • 任何模拟框架或生成模型（CARLA、Helios++、OpenScene、神经辐射场、扩散模型、生成对抗网络、自定义物理引擎）。开源或闭源均可 — 关键在于合成数据。

pages.title: Description
pages.content:
# 🩺 
# **OncoSegment: Breast Tumor Mapping Challenge**

# 💡 
## **Why this Problem is Interesting**

Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of death among women worldwide. Early and accurate detection through ultrasound is critical, but interpreting these images is notoriously difficult.Ultrasound images suffer from "speckle noise" and low contrast. Much like the "blobs" in plasma physics simulations, tumors in ultrasound are intermittent, have irregular boundaries, and can be easily confused with healthy tissue. This challenge asks you to develop an AI that can precisely outline tumor boundaries, a task that directly assists radiologists in biopsy planning and treatment.

# 📊 
## **The Data**

The dataset is derived from the Breast Ultrasound Images (BUSI) collection, featuring women aged 25–75. It consists of high-quality PNG scans with a standard resolution (approx. 500x500 px).

Dataset Breakdown:

Benign: Tumors that are typically oval or round with smooth edges.

Malignant: Cancerous tumors, often characterized by "spiky" (spiculated) or irregular borders that invade surrounding tissue.

Normal: Scans with no tumors (used to test your model's ability to avoid False Positives).

What you receive in the Starting Kit:
train_images: A list of PIL images (Grayscale) showing the breast 
tissue.
train_masks: Binary masks where 1 represents the tumor and 0 represents the background.
train_labels: Metadata identifying the tumor as benign or malignant.
test_images: Images where you must predict the mask.

 # 📏 
## **Metrics: Measuring Precision**

In medical imaging, a "box" is not enough. We need to know exactly which pixels are cancerous. We use two complementary overlap metrics:
1. Primary Metric: Dice Coefficient (F1-Score)The Dice coefficient is the gold standard for medical segmentation. It is twice the area of overlap divided by the total number of pixels in both the prediction and the ground truth.
$$Dice = \frac{2 \times |P \cap G|}{|P| + |G|}$$
Why? It is highly sensitive to the internal "fullness" of the mask and rewards models that get the shape exactly right.
2. Secondary Metric: Jaccard Index (IoU)
The Jaccard index is the area of intersection divided by the area of union.
$$Jaccard = \frac{|P \cap G|}{|P \cup G|}$$
Why? 
It is more "punishing" than Dice for small errors.
It helps break ties on the leaderboard by highlighting models with the fewest stray False Positive pixels.
pages.content_zh:
# 🩺 
# **OncoSegment：乳腺肿瘤分割挑战赛**

# 💡 
## **为什么这个问题很有意义**

乳腺癌仍然是全球女性死亡的主要原因之一。通过超声进行早期准确检测至关重要，但解读这些图像出了名的困难。超声图像存在"散斑噪声"和对比度低的问题。就像等离子体物理模拟中的"团块"一样，超声中的肿瘤呈散在分布，边界不规则，很容易与健康组织混淆。本挑战赛要求你开发一种能够精确勾画肿瘤边界的AI，这项任务直接协助放射科医生进行活检规划和治疗。

# 📊 
## **数据**

该数据集源自乳腺超声图像（BUSI）数据集，涵盖25-75岁女性。它由高质量的PNG扫描图像组成，标准分辨率约为500×500像素。

数据集分类：

良性：通常为椭圆形或圆形、边缘光滑的肿瘤。

恶性：癌性肿瘤，通常以"棘状"（毛刺状）或不规则边界为特征，侵袭周围组织。

正常：没有肿瘤的扫描图像（用于测试模型避免假阳性的能力）。

入门套件提供的内容：
train_images：一组显示乳腺组织的PIL图像（灰度）。
train_masks：二值掩膜，其中1代表肿瘤，0代表背景。
train_labels：识别肿瘤为良性或恶性的元数据。
test_images：你需要预测其掩膜的图像。

 # 📏 
## **评估指标：衡量精确度**

在医学影像中，仅用一个"框"是不够的。我们需要准确知道哪些像素是癌变的。我们使用两种互补的重叠指标：
1. 主要指标：Dice系数（F1分数）Dice系数是医学分割的金标准。它是预测掩膜与真实掩膜重叠区域面积的两倍，除以两者像素总数。
$$Dice = \frac{2 \times |P \cap G|}{|P| + |G|}$$
为什么？它对掩膜内部的"饱满度"非常敏感，并奖励那些能准确把握形状的模型。
2. 次要指标：Jaccard指数（IoU）
Jaccard指数是交集面积除以并集面积。
$$Jaccard = \frac{|P \cap G|}{|P \cup G|}$$
为什么？
对于微小的错误，它比Dice更"惩罚性强"。
它通过突出显示具有最少游离假阳性像素的模型，帮助在排行榜上打破平局。
